summary: Hard-valid queue-aware Binance Futures fair-value shock to Bybit post-only entry screen. Event counts were ample on train/calibration but actual conservative fills were too sparse and unstable to fit the frozen two-stage model. At 100ms, train/calibration/confirmation produced 3385/507/52 events and 28/6/0 fills. At 300ms, 3238/485/51 events produced 15/0/0 fills. The filled training paths were far below even the minimum 12bp cost: mean gross 0.3863bp at 100ms and 0.7635bp at 300ms. The exact information unit is retired without threshold, queue, latency, model, target, risk or leverage tuning.

100ms.failure_reason: insufficient filled outcomes for conditional model

300ms.failure_reason: fill outcome has only one class

cost_diagnostic.economic_interpretation: Passive entry removed one taker leg in concept, but conservative queue fills occurred only after the external edge had mostly decayed; gross filled expectancy remained less than one basis point and could not support the cost contract.

retirement_boundary: Do not tune adjacent shock/gap thresholds, queue participation, quote-identity rule, latency, model, calibration, target, stop, risk or leverage under this information unit. The repeated lesson is structural: at current public best-quote queue priority, fill arrives after edge decay. A subsequent passive-entry hypothesis must materially change queue priority or venue/order mechanism, not loosen this screen.
